site.heroDescription: Fresh breakfasts. Good leftovers. A little less thinking about what to eat.
site.planAside: A little variety. A simple rhythm.
site.recipeIntro: Fresh recipes are portioned per person; batch recipes are scaled to the meals in this plan.
site.targetNote: Targets, not exact totals. Portions and brands matter.
site.workoutNote: Include your **Fairlife shake — 30 g protein, 150 calories** in the snack. Use 170 g yogurt + berries, or half a cottage cheese snack. Keep the breakfast shake separate.
site.nutritionNote: Nutrition is approximate, based on source recipe cards and typical ingredient labels. Ham, mixed vegetables, dairy and powder change the totals. Log your actual brands if precision matters.
site.shoppingNote: Shopping quantities are calculated from this plan. Full-size rest-day snacks are included; workout swaps may leave extras.
site.storageNote: Keep cold toppings and crunchy snack toppings separate.
site.storageSafety: Refrigerate cooked food within 2 hours at 40°F / 4°C or below. Use leftovers within 3–4 days; reheat to 165°F / 74°C.

oats.title: Apple & brown sugar steel-cut oats + two lattes
oats.description: Warm oats, a chopped apple, and a little richness, with your two morning lattes. Your smaller protein shake stays on the side.

ingredients.label: dry steel-cut oats + water per package
plain Fairlife or MooTopia 2% milk for two lattes per person
Coffee or espresso, as you prefer

steps: Simmer the oats in water for the time on your package, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the apple near the end for softer fruit, or add it fresh. Finish with brown sugar and butter or half-and-half.
Shake the powder with water separately. Use its label to measure the listed protein amount; this is protein content, not powder weight.
Make two lattes per person, dividing the listed milk equally between them. Add your coffee or espresso; no syrup or sugar is included.
oats.note: Measure oats dry; use your powder and dairy labels for tracking. Nutrition includes both lattes, estimated with Fairlife 2% at 120 calories and 13 g protein per 8 fl oz. Use your MooTopia carton label if it differs. The latte milk replaces about 20 g protein from the original 40 g protein shake; the remaining shake provides 20 g protein. The food portion stays at 60 g dry oats.

ham.title: Ham frittata, toast + two lattes
ham.description: A smaller ham frittata and a slice of toast, with your two morning lattes included in the breakfast estimate.

ingredients.label: plain Fairlife or MooTopia 2% milk for two lattes per person
Coffee or espresso, as you prefer

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F / 175°C. Coat a small oven-safe skillet with cooking spray; warm the ham.
Whisk eggs, cottage cheese, Parmesan and spinach. Pour into the skillet, cook briefly to set the base, then bake until fully set (about 16–18 minutes; 160°F / 71°C in the center).
Slice the frittata into {portionsWord} equal portions and serve with the toast. Ham and Parmesan add salt; season to taste.
Make two lattes per person, dividing the listed milk equally between them. Add your coffee or espresso; no syrup or sugar is included.
ham.note: Ham replaces the Italian chicken sausage; its label determines the final calories. Nutrition includes both lattes, estimated with Fairlife 2% at 120 calories and 13 g protein per 8 fl oz. Use your MooTopia carton label if it differs.

buffalo.title: Buffalo chicken rice bowls
buffalo.description: Chicken, black beans and brown rice with buffalo sauce and melted cheddar.
steps: Cook the onion in the listed cooking oil until softened. Stir in beans, paprika and cumin.
In a sprayed skillet, cook chicken to 165°F / 74°C. Toss with buffalo sauce.
Split rice, beans, chicken and cheddar between {portionsWord} containers. Divide the oil for portions equally between the rice/bean portions; finish with scallions.
buffalo.note: The extra olive oil is included in the calorie estimate.

greek.title: Greek chicken rice bowls
greek.description: Lemon-oregano chicken with rice, crunchy vegetables, olives and feta.
steps: Flatten chicken to an even thickness. Marinate in lemon juice, vinegar, marinade oil, garlic and oregano for 30 minutes in the fridge.
Cook rice with broth according to its package. Grill or pan-cook chicken to 165°F / 74°C; rest and slice.
Split chicken and rice between {portionsWord} portions. Pack chopped vegetables, olives and feta separately. At serving, add the toppings, remaining oil and lemon.
greek.note: Reheat only chicken and rice; add the cold toppings afterward.

honey.title: Honey garlic chicken thighs
honey.description: Glazed chicken thighs, rice and easy frozen mixed vegetables.
steps: Mix sauces, honey, sesame oil and garlic. Coat chicken and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roast at 425°F / 220°C on a lined tray; add onion and finish under the broiler for color. Check chicken reaches 165°F / 74°C; watch the broiler closely.
Heat vegetables and rice. Divide all food equally into {portionsWord} dinner containers.
honey.note: Mixed vegetables replace broccoli, so actual nutrition varies slightly.

source.label: Adapted from The Meal Prep Manual

chile.title: Chile lemon chicken rice bowls
chile.description: Yogurt-seasoned thighs with peppers, cabbage, tomato and rice.

ingredients.label: each chili powder, onion powder and garlic powder for chicken
each chili and onion powder for vegetables

steps: Coat thighs with yogurt, chicken spices and lemon juice. Roast at 425°F / 220°C; broil briefly for browning. Check 165°F / 74°C before slicing.
Heat oil, garlic and vegetable spices in a skillet. Add diced peppers and onion; soften, then add cabbage and tomato sauce.
Stir in rice, sliced chicken and remaining lemon juice. Divide evenly into {portionsWord} containers.
chile.note: Bagged shredded cabbage keeps preparation simple.

source.label: Adapted from The Meal Prep Manual

yogurt.title: Greek yogurt, berries & walnuts
yogurt.description: A quick yogurt bowl with fruit, honey and a little crunch.
steps: Spoon yogurt into a bowl. Add berries, honey and walnuts just before eating.
yogurt.note: Workout version: 170 g yogurt + ½ cup berries + one Fairlife shake (30 g protein / 150 calories). Skip honey and walnuts. About 290–310 calories total.

cottage.title: Whipped cottage cheese & berries
cottage.description: Smooth cottage cheese topped with berries and slivered almonds.
steps: Blend cottage cheese, vanilla and sweetener until smooth.
Divide into {portionsWord} bowls; top each with an equal share of the berries and almonds.
cottage.note: Workout version: half of one full-size snack + one Fairlife shake (30 g protein / 150 calories), about 315 calories. The grocery list covers full-size snacks.

steps: Spoon yogurt into a bowl. Add berries, honey and walnuts just before eating.
yogurt-1800.note: Rest-day snack. For a workout, use 100 g yogurt and the listed berries with a 30 g / 150 calorie Fairlife shake; skip the walnuts and honey. The workout version is about 250 calories.

taco-mac.title: One-pot Taco Mac
taco-mac.description: A new batch recipe for this meal-plan variation.
steps: Brown beef in oil, breaking it up; add peppers and green onion whites. Cook beef through, then stir in the seasonings.
Add tomatoes, broth and dry macaroni. Cover and simmer 10–12 minutes, stirring midway, until pasta is tender; add water if needed.
Stir in milk off the heat. Divide into {portionsWord} portions and top with cheddar and green onion tops.
taco-mac.note: Source portion size retained. Estimate uses 93/7 beef and regular cheese; your milk and cheese labels may change it.

source.label: Adapted from The Meal Prep Manual

teriyaki-beef.title: Teriyaki beef & vegetable rice bowls
teriyaki-beef.description: A new batch recipe for this meal-plan variation.
steps: Cook the listed rice amount. Dice vegetables; slice the onion.
Brown beef with a little of the oil until cooked through; set aside. Use remaining oil to sauté vegetables and garlic until just tender.
Return beef, add teriyaki sauce and heat through. Divide rice and beef mixture into {portionsWord} portions.
teriyaki-beef.note: Source portion size retained. Estimate uses 90/10 beef; bottled sauce brands vary.

source.label: Adapted from The Meal Prep Manual

cilantro-lime.title: Creamy cilantro lime chicken bowls
cilantro-lime.description: A new batch recipe for this meal-plan variation.

ingredients.label: garlic powder; reserve one-third for sauce
each onion powder and chili powder

steps: Heat oven to 400°F. Coat thighs with paprika, chicken spices, a little lime and one-third of the oil. Roast until 165°F, about 25–35 minutes.
Roast diced sweet potato with another third of the oil until tender. Cook mixed vegetables per package; prepare the rice.
Blend yogurt, cilantro, green onion, jalapeño, cumin, reserved garlic, remaining lime and oil; thin with water.
Divide chicken, vegetables and rice into {portionsWord} portions; store sauce separately.
cilantro-lime.note: Larger source portion with rounded amounts; mixed vegetables replace broccoli. Calories are an adapted estimate.

source.label: Adapted from The Meal Prep Manual

sriracha-lime.title: Sriracha lime chicken & sweet potato bowls
sriracha-lime.description: A new batch recipe for this meal-plan variation.

ingredients.label: each onion powder and garlic powder

steps: Heat oven to 400°F. Mix sriracha, lime, honey and seasonings. Reserve half separately; coat thighs with the rest.
Roast chicken until 165°F, about 25–35 minutes. Roast diced sweet potatoes with half the oil until tender; prepare rice.
Cook mixed vegetables per package, then sauté briefly with green onion whites and remaining oil. Add reserved sauce, diced chicken, potatoes and rice.
Divide into {portionsWord} portions; top with green onion greens.
sriracha-lime.note: Rounded source quantities with mixed vegetables replacing broccoli. Use a mild sauce or reduce sriracha for less heat.

source.label: Adapted from The Meal Prep Manual

cherry-pork.title: Cherry-balsamic pork, rice & vegetables
cherry-pork.description: A new batch recipe for this meal-plan variation.

ingredients.label: fresh thyme, or less dried thyme

steps: Heat oven to 400°F. Simmer balsamic until reduced, then stir in preserves and thyme.
Season trimmed pork with garlic, salt and pepper. Sear in an oven-safe skillet with cooking spray; add half the glaze.
Roast until 145°F, then rest 10 minutes before slicing. Cook rice and mixed vegetables separately.
Divide pork, rice, vegetables and remaining glaze into {portionsWord} portions.
cherry-pork.note: Each meal uses 1½ source pork portions, plus rice and mixed vegetables. Side estimates assume 195 calories per cooked rice cup and 50 per 100 g vegetables.

Fresh or dried; use less if dried

measurementNotes: Recipe quantities describe the base number of servings. Fresh preparations keep that portion size; batch recipes scale to the selected plan.
Rice shopping assumes 180 g dry per cup and a 3:1 cooked-to-dry volume yield; follow your package for actual yields.
Berries use about 150 g per cup. Garlic uses about 1 clove per teaspoon minced and 10 cloves per head. Lemons assume 2 tablespoons juice each, plus the measured lemon for wedges.
Shopping amounts round up to the configured increment or package size. Fraction strings such as "2/3" keep quantity calculations exact.

Breakfast assumes two lattes per person daily, each using 6 fl oz plain 2% ultra-filtered milk. Nutrition estimates use Fairlife: 120 calories and 13 g protein per 8 fl oz. MooTopia labels may differ; no syrup or added sugar is included. Fairlife milk label: https://fairlife.com/ultra-filtered-milk/reduced-fat-2-percent-milk/

New variation nutrition uses source recipe cards with rounded portions. Mixed vegetables are estimated at 50 calories per 100 g instead of broccoli at about 34. White rice shopping uses the same 180 g dry per cup and 3:1 volume yield assumption; follow your package. Meat gram conversion uses 454 g per pound.
